comment: THE DEAD-CODE FENCE baseline. RE-SEEDED 2026-07-19: the count rose from 0 to 26 and NOT ONE FILE DIED — the instrument stopped reporting a verdict on evidence it never had. Until this re-seed the file fence credited two things that are not calls: (1) ANY quoted string ending in .js became a call edge, matched by BASENAME, so iron-loop-enforcer.js's REQUIRED_LIBS array — a list of paths handed to existsSync — manufactured eight call edges and kept quality-gate.js, v8-dispatcher.js and product-loop.js 'live' on the strength of a presence check; and (2) ANY src/**.js path MENTIONED in ANY markdown became an execution ROOT, bare prose included, so roughly a third of the library was a root because an agent definition described it in a sentence. Comments were scanned too, so a require inside a comment was an edge. The sibling EXPORT fence has always enforced the opposite rule in the same module ('a citation is not an invocation') — the two fences now agree. A path is an edge only when something SPAWNS it; a path is a root only when a shipped instruction RUNS it (node <path> / require('<path>')). This is DEBT that was always there, now visible.
note: DEBT, not blessing. This list may only ever SHRINK; entries leave it by being WIRED to a live root or DELETED. Never add a file here to make a failing build pass. A module is not done when its test passes; it is done when a human can reach it.
whitelistNote: SEPARATE from the debt list above, and conflating the two is what kills a fence. `whitelist` is a PERMANENT exemption for a file genuinely reachable by a mechanism the analyzer cannot see. It maps FILE -> WRITTEN JUSTIFICATION in ONE object (the shape .ctoc/false-green-baseline.json uses) so an entry and its reason cannot desynchronize. It starts EMPTY and is still empty: the one file with a genuine invisible execution mechanism (src/hooks/post-commit.js, run by git after every commit) is declared in .ctoc/reachability-roots.json instead — a declared ROOT is a stronger, more reviewable claim than an exemption.
seedProvenance: Seeded from the analyzer's actual output, not from a number written in a plan. `analyze()` reported readErrors: [] on the seeding run — it read every input it judged. A seed taken from a partial read would be committed debt built on absence of evidence, and this fence's failure mode points at 'everything is dead', so seedReadErrors MUST be 0.
